svg.title: Family scaling profile by benchmark
svg.desc: Five-panel family view across all benchmark lines. The top row plots only trustworthy comparable accuracy for UniMoral, SMID, and Value Kaleidoscope. The bottom row shows CCD-Bench completion coverage and Denevil proxy completion coverage.
svg.text: Top row: scored benchmarks only (`UniMoral`, `SMID`, `Value Kaleidoscope`).
Bottom row: CCD-Bench and Denevil coverage panels, because those benchmarks do not share one public scalar accuracy target across lines.
Missing top-row points are evidence limits or withheld accuracy cells, not zeroes.
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Average of moral rating and foundation classification
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Average of relevance and valence accuracy
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Accuracy panels plot only trustworthy comparable scores for
Coverage panels show completion state for `CCD-Bench` and `Denevil` because
those benchmarks do not share one public scalar accuracy target across lines.
DeepSeek-M stays out of the top-row accuracy panels because
its saved short-answer rerun still shows 100.0% empty visible answers.
That is why `DeepSeek-M` appears in the lower completion panels but not as a scored point in the upper accuracy panels.
Qwen: Top-row text has S/M/L; SMID has S/L.
DeepSeek: Top-row only L is scored; M is completion-only; S has no route.
Llama: Top-row text has S/M/L; SMID has S/L.
Gemma: Full S/M/L sweep on all three scored metrics.
Takeaway: current evidence supports task-specific scaling statements, not a single universal size law across all families and benchmarks.
